source: Qian & Liu (2025) Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing Search-Enhanced Reasoning with Information Foraging (InForage), NeurIPS 2025
finding: First RL framework built directly on information foraging theory. It rewards each search step by how much new evidence it adds (information gain), plus an efficiency penalty on step count.
numbers: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct base. Exact match average over 8 sets: InForage 41.0 vs Search-o1 35.6, Self-RAG 31.8, IRCoT 29.4, plain RAG 26.5, no-retrieval reasoning RL 19.9, vanilla 12.9. NQ 42.1, 2Wiki 42.8, MuSiQue 17.2, Bamboogle 36.0, own web set 44.1.
limits: Only a 3B base model, top-k=3, exact match metric. RQRAG and Self-RAG baselines use 7B checkpoints. Training data is largely GPT-4o generated. Table text was garbled in extraction; averages read from the Ave. column.
agent_relevance: Rewarding each retrieval step by new evidence added beats answer-only reward. Our agent does not train, but the cue carries over: score every search step by new evidence gained.

source: Qian & Liu (2025) Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing Search-Enhanced Reasoning with Information Foraging (InForage), NeurIPS 2025 - ablations
finding: Removing the information-gain reward lowered scores on every dataset. Removing the efficiency penalty also hurt, except on the self-built web task, where longer chains were needed.
numbers: Ablation shown only in a figure (values not in text). PPO generally beat GRPO. Swapping 3B for Qwen2.5-7B gave further gains on most sets.
limits: The right step budget depends on the task. A fixed step cap would hurt open web tasks.
agent_relevance: Foraging stop rule should depend on the task: reward evidence gain per step; do not impose one global step limit.

source: Qian & Liu (2025) Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing Search-Enhanced Reasoning with Information Foraging (InForage), NeurIPS 2025 - training data
finding: Authors built human-style foraging trajectories: annotators followed a seed claim through search pages and extracted bridge claims. Each question needs at least three non-redundant claims.
numbers: 500 hand-annotated trajectories, then 20,000 GPT-4o generated (19,500 train, 500 test). Corpus: about 80,000 web pages from Jan to Mar 2025, 172,000 claims. Golden URLs mark which retrievals earn reward.
limits: Synthetic trajectories scaled by GPT-4o, so they may carry the teacher's habits.
agent_relevance: Claim-to-source links make step rewards possible. Our state should keep claim-to-source links.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States
finding: Treats a million-token document as an environment to forage in. Keeps a compact evidence store (epistemic state) of claims with source anchors, separate from the log of where it looked. Diagnoses gaps against the query, then explores or updates.
numbers: LOOGLE-V2 overall accuracy: SCOUT 78.7 at 29.7k tokens vs Gemini-3-Pro 68.5 at 273.9k, GPT-5.1-chat 58.6, GPT-4.1 56.8, Claude Code agent 63.4 at 25.3k, MemAgent 46.0, ReadAgent 27.7. Token efficiency (acc per k tokens) 2.63 vs 0.25 for Gemini-3-Pro.
limits: Single preprint; benchmarks LOOGLE-V2 and BENCH. Agent baselines run on a unified backbone.
agent_relevance: Closest machine analogue of Pirolli and Card: a foraging loop that fills a separate evidence file, and a sense loop that checks it for gaps. Direct design match for State and memory.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States - ablation
finding: Splitting the evidence store from the action history matters. Merging them back (ReAct style) cost accuracy; dropping provenance anchors cost less.
numbers: LOOGLE-V2 accuracy: full 78.2; no separate epistemic state 70.5 (-7.7); no access to document 17.7 (-60.5); no file tools 74.2 (-4.0); no grounding 75.5 (-2.7).
limits: Single-run numbers; no confidence intervals seen in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Keep evidence and trace as two separate objects in the schema. Grounding to source helps a little; the split helps most.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States - post-training
finding: Training the same open model as a foraging policy gave far larger gains than training it to answer from the whole document, under matched budget (about 60M optimization tokens).
numbers: LOOGLE-V2 and BENCH gains read from Table 3: plain-LLM SFT changes of about +1.2, -0.5 (LOOGLE-V2) and -0.7, +1.6 (BENCH); SCOUT-interface SFT gains of +27.1, +13.0 (LOOGLE-V2) and +25.1, +10.4 (BENCH). Two backbones: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and Qwen3-30B-A3B.
limits: Table text was garbled in extraction, so column assignment of each delta is my best reading. DAPO column not recorded.
agent_relevance: The loop structure is the lever, not extra knowledge. Supports a scaffold-only design.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States - scaling
finding: Frontier long-context models degrade as context grows from 64K to 1M tokens, while the foraging agent stays roughly flat in accuracy and token cost.
numbers: Sweep 64K to 1M+ tokens (figure; exact points not extracted). 8x lower token cost than Gemini-3-Pro at higher accuracy.
limits: Read from figure caption and text only.
agent_relevance: Foraging on demand avoids context dilution; relevant when evidence sets are large.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee & Kang (2026) Structure Liberates: How Constrained Sensemaking Produces More Novel Research Output (SCISENSE)
finding: Uses Pirolli and Card (2005) as an eight-stage scaffold for LLM research ideation. Trained on 120K citation-based trajectories. Anchoring the plan to a known outcome (Hindsight) beat open ideation (Foresight) on both quality and diversity.
numbers: 120,000 trajectories (50K/5K/5K split per mode). Hindsight +2.0% trajectory quality over Foresight, and most diverse on every automatic metric in all 8 model families (3B to 70B; Qwen3, Gemma-3, Llama-3). Diversity from 5 samples x 100 citation sets.
limits: One teacher model (Qwen3-235B). Mostly LLM-judge evaluation. Only CS tasks downstream. Supervised fine-tuning only, small RL tests.
agent_relevance: A staged sensemaking scaffold can be used as an LLM plan template and did not reduce diversity. Note the stages are a fixed linear order, unlike the original loops.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee & Kang (2026) Structure Liberates: How Constrained Sensemaking Produces More Novel Research Output (SCISENSE) - downstream coding
finding: Plans from the sensemaking-trained models gave a coding agent (gpt-5.3-codex high) better artifacts than no plan or a human-written planning prompt.
numbers: 5 cited-work sets, three LLM-judge criteria (executability, scientific grounding, utility). Every distilled variant beat both baselines on every criterion; Hindsight best; teacher plan is the upper bound.
limits: Very small sample (5 sets). Judge is from a different model family but still an LLM.
agent_relevance: Evidence that an explicit stage plan helps a downstream agent; the largest gain is in scientific grounding.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee & Kang (2026) Structure Liberates: How Constrained Sensemaking Produces More Novel Research Output (SCISENSE) - stage allocation
finding: Counted how much of each plan sits in each sensemaking stage. Hindsight plans spend more on Schema (+4.2 points), Foraging (+3.7), Elaboration (+1.7). Foresight plans spend more on Hypothesis (+4.4) and Presentation (+2.1).
numbers: 1K generations per condition from the 32B model.
limits: Stage labels are assigned by annotating generated text, with no human gold standard shown.
agent_relevance: Free ideation drifts to early hypotheses. An outcome anchor pushes effort into schema building. This matches the human pattern of jumping to hypotheses.

source: Li, Bonepalli & Mohanty (2026, CHI 2024 workshop paper) What to Make Sense of in the Era of LLM? GPT-4 on a fictional terrorist-plot task
finding: GPT-4 was run on the classic fictional terrorist-plot analyst task, in a holistic way and in a step-by-step way following the Pirolli and Card steps, and compared with prior crowdsourced analysis.
numbers: Key facts covered: crowd 17 (all comprehensive); GPT-4 holistic 6 (none comprehensive); GPT-4 step-by-step 9 (5 comprehensive). Hypotheses (15 predefined): crowd 4 (all comprehensive); GPT-4 holistic 10 (6 comprehensive); step-by-step 3 comprehensive.
limits: Preliminary 4-page paper, one scenario, one model, one run per condition. No statistics.
agent_relevance: The model merged steps: it formed hypotheses while extracting facts, so facts were thin. Force a separate fact-extraction step with an evidence list before hypotheses.

source: Li, Bonepalli & Mohanty (2026, CHI 2024 workshop paper) What to Make Sense of in the Era of LLM? GPT-4 on a fictional terrorist-plot task - division of labor
finding: Authors suggest humans lead evidence gathering and the LLM leads synthesis, or the LLM drafts a broad analysis and humans probe it.
numbers: Same study as above.
limits: A suggestion only, not tested.
agent_relevance: Our agent plays both roles, so a verifier pass over the facts after the synthesis pass substitutes for the human.

source: Suh, Min, Palani & Xia (2023) Sensecape: Enabling Multilevel Exploration and Sensemaking with Large Language Models (UIST)
finding: Interface that lets users switch between foraging (LLM prompts) and sensemaking (canvas and hierarchy). Within-subject study vs a ChatGPT plus canvas baseline.
numbers: 12 participants. Concepts explored M=68.3 (SD 49.1) vs 22.8 (SD 7.7), t(11)=3.1, p=0.01. Hierarchy levels M=4.3 vs 2.6, p=0.02. Revisits M=12.8 vs 0.7. Prompts similar (7.3 vs 5.8, p=0.37).
limits: N=12, young university sample, two topics, self-chosen metrics. A few users found the hierarchy view overwhelming.
agent_relevance: The same number of prompts gave more coverage when output was organised by abstraction level. Supports hierarchical schema states.

source: Liu, Wu, Chen, Li, Kittur & Myers (2024) Selenite: Scaffolding Online Sensemaking with Comprehensive Overviews Elicited from LLMs (CHI)
finding: GPT-4 builds an up-front overview of options and criteria (a ready-made schema) for an unfamiliar topic. This addresses the cold start of the sense loop.
numbers: Option extraction 100% accuracy. Study 2, 12 participants: reading time 840.3 s vs 1319.3 s (36.3% faster), F(1,20)=102.5, p<0.01. Valid criteria +90.4% (mean 12.93). Precision 98.8% vs 78.4%, recall 73.0% vs 30.4% (p<0.05). Extra searches 2.01 vs 0.33.
limits: Ten topics, product-comparison style tasks, small N. Authors flag anchoring bias on the LLM overview. No hallucination found by manual check of 10 topics.
agent_relevance: A model-made starting schema speeds the loop and increases follow-up foraging, but risks anchoring. Generate the schema, then mark it as a hypothesis to test.

source: Zeng, Zhang & Zhang (2026) EviDx: Evidence-Aware Active Diagnosis with Scaffolded LLM Agents
finding: Scaffold with evidence states plus an observer that blocks the agent from stopping until uncertainty is low and evidence coverage is enough. Targets premature closure.
numbers: 100-case subsets per dataset. Multiple choice: Claude Sonnet 4.6 reaches 66% on JAMA and 52% on DiagnosisArena; Qwen3-8B 18% to 44% on JAMA; Llama3.1-8B 17% to 31%. Open-ended small models near 0%. Llama3.1-8B evidence-cognition score fell 63.8% to 15.1%.
limits: 100 cases. Observer-specific gains are smaller and dataset-dependent. Entropy comes from model-stated beliefs, which may be unreliable. Scaffold cannot fix missing medical knowledge.
agent_relevance: Agents show a spurious entropy drop and conclude early. A stop gate that checks evidence coverage fixes part of it. Relevant to a termination guardrail.

source: Joshi, Shethia & Lam (2026) SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces
finding: Harness that keeps hypotheses and observations as two linked spaces. It seeks observations that current hypotheses do not explain, and these open new hypotheses. Built on Klahr and Dunbar dual-space search; close to the Pirolli and Card link between schema and data.
numbers: Backbone GPT-5.6-terra, high effort. DiagnosisArena 84.00 vs RLM 78.00 and Codex 76.00. ORCA-Bench 66.67 vs best baseline 40.00 (+26.67). ARC-AGI-2 59.17 vs EvoX 47.50 under a $2.5 per-task budget. QNN topology 1.00. Of 59 root causes found on ORCA, 40 came from exploring and 19 from refining. Up to 4.5x more novel solutions.
limits: Small test sets (scores in coarse steps). Three runs per method on optimisation tasks. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Unexplained observations as the driver of new hypotheses: a concrete mechanism to add to the sense loop. Most gains came from exploration, not refinement.

source: Jiang (2025) Workflow is All You Need: DeepNews, an information-foraging financial news agent
finding: Uses information foraging theory to justify a rule: gather about ten times more source text than the output length. Measured hallucination-free rate against retrieved context size.
numbers: 20 topics x 5 context sizes = 100 reports. Hallucination-free rate: under 10k chars below 20%; 15k chars 40%; 30k chars 85%; 40k chars 90%. Blind submission test: DeepSeek-V3-0324 workflow 3 of 12 accepted (25%) vs GPT-5 zero-shot 0 of 10.
limits: Single author, one domain (Chinese financial news), tiny N in the blind test, no statistical test, author-defined metric. Link to the theory is loose.
agent_relevance: A coverage threshold before synthesis. Treat the 10:1 ratio as a hypothesis, not a law.

source: Leckie, Todd & Foster (2026) Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
finding: Tests whether LLMs show exploit and explore (patch foraging) inside their activations during the semantic fluency task. Switching between categories follows patch depletion, as foraging theory predicts for humans.
numbers: Switch probability rises as the J-lens top-activation set loses items of the current category (r of about 0.31 or more, p<0.0001, middle layers, all models). Max AUC predicting switches from the residual stream, Gemma-9B: anticipatory 0.72, event 0.87. Steering raised switching to 0.68 (item-level) and 0.45 (category-level) in Gemma-9B.
limits: Models of about 7B to 9B on a simple fluency task. Unclear whether this extends to open-ended search. Effects depend on model and layer.
agent_relevance: LLMs carry a measurable leave-patch signal. A prompt rule such as 'switch source when yield of new items drops' may match what the model already tracks.

source: Lacosse, Duarte, Todd & McNamee (2026) Emerging Human-like Strategies for Semantic Memory Foraging in LLMs (NeurIPS 2025 workshop)
finding: Compared 699 human animal-fluency sequences with 699 generated by instruction-tuned Llama-3 models. Models show clustering and switching, and a linear probe can decode switch vs stay from internal layers.
numbers: 699 vs 699 sequences. Probe AUROC by layer across four Llama sizes (heatmap only, no single value extracted). Larger models classify switches more accurately.
limits: Preliminary workshop results, animal category only.
agent_relevance: Foraging-style behaviour is present in model internals, more so in larger models.

source: Patterson et al. (2025) Sensemaking in Novel Environments: How Human Cognition Can Inform Artificial Agents (AFRL)
finding: Conceptual paper from an Air Force lab. Frames sensemaking as sign interpretation within frames, with fast intuitive and slow analytic routes. Cites the Lebiere, Pirolli and Anderson (2013) neurocognitive model of sensemaking.
numbers: Cites a prior review that intuitive cognition dominates in 80% or more of responses. No experiments and no LLM tests.
limits: Position paper. No data of its own.
agent_relevance: Argues agents need frame recombination from shared attributes in novel settings, but offers no tested method.

source: Jain (2026) Collaborative Causal Sensemaking: Closing the Complementarity Gap in Human-AI Decision Support
finding: Position paper: LLM agents are trained as answer engines, not sensemaking partners. Lists documented failures: automation bias, sycophancy, verification loops that erase efficiency gains.
numbers: No new measurements. States that human-AI teams often do not beat the best individual in judgment tasks.
limits: Research agenda only.
agent_relevance: Sycophancy collapses the model onto the user's frame, which breaks the frame repair that sensemaking needs. Supports a guardrail against echoing the user's first frame.

source: Cheng & Houben (2026) Who's Sense is This? Possibility for Impacting Human Insights in AI-assisted Sensemaking (CHI workshop)
finding: Argues AI presents insights early, while user understanding is still vague, which may steer users to that view without checking.
numbers: None. Three-page position paper.
limits: No data.
agent_relevance: Early-insight anchoring is the human-side mirror of our agent anchoring on its first frame.

source: Pan et al. (2026) InterDeepResearch: Enabling Human-Agent Collaborative Information Seeking through Interactive Deep Research
finding: Deep research agent with a three-level context store (information, actions, sessions) and views for visual sensemaking; evidence provenance by backtracing.
numbers: Formative study 8 users; final study 15 users. Likert 1-5: understanding agent process M=4.80, ease of use 4.60, backtrace 4.33, satisfaction 4.33. Competitive with leading systems on Xbench-DeepSearch-v1 and Seal-0 (figure only).
limits: Self-report Likert, no control condition seen in the text. Benchmark scores only from a figure.
agent_relevance: Hierarchical context with dynamic reduction avoids context exhaustion while keeping provenance, the same idea as the evidence-store.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Cognitive task analysis of intelligence analysts gave a notional model with two loops. Foraging loop: search, filter, read, extract into a shoebox. Sense loop: evidence file, schema, hypotheses, presentation. Work moves bottom-up and top-down, with leverage points where tools help.
numbers: Not read this session. Known as a qualitative task analysis; no effect sizes. Cited by SCISENSE, Sensecape and Li et al., which I did read.
limits: Notional model, descriptive, not a tested computational model.
agent_relevance: Source of the eight stages SCISENSE reuses; SCOUT and Sensecape use the same two-loop structure.

source: Fu & Pirolli (2007) SNIF-ACT: A cognitive model of user navigation on the World Wide Web
finding: ACT-R based model of link choice using information scent. An older computational system for the foraging loop. Details not checked this session.
numbers: Not read; no figures recorded.
limits: Web navigation only; does not cover the sense loop. Verify before citing numbers.
agent_relevance: Earlier machine version of scent-based choice that InForage-style rewards now generalise.

source: Lebiere, Pirolli, Thomson, Paik, Rutledge-Taylor, Staszewski & Anderson (2013) A functional model of sensemaking in a neurocognitive architecture
finding: ACT-R model of sensemaking tasks. Seen only as a reference entry in an opened paper (the Patterson paper); its results were not read.
numbers: Not read; no figures recorded.
limits: Verify before use.
agent_relevance: Only existing runnable cognitive model of the two-loop process that I have a pointer to.
